title: The Sigil of Ashvale Anew
premise: Petra Dravenmoor, memory-thief and reluctant bookkeeper for the Ashvale Guild of impossible trades, discovers the ledgers hide a contract selling a child's soul to the court beneath the mountain. As the old gods stir and answer prayers, the guild's power fractures, and Petra's own stolen memories begin surfacing, revealing she was the first soul ever sold. To save the child, she must infiltrate the subterranean court, confront the god-king who bought her past, and choose between restoring her stolen self and destroying the contract that binds them both. She burns her own memories to unmake the ledger, freeing the child but losing herself, until the grateful gods, newly awakened, return what she gave away as their first answered prayer.
about_author: Wren Ishikawa is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing confiscated grimoires before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about people who trade in things that should never be for sale.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. In the guild's candlelit counting house, Petra balances accounts of traded shadows, borrowed years, and bottled names, hiding her own thefts in the margins. A routine audit reveals an entry she never wrote: a soul, sold, sealed. Emotional beat: quiet dread as her invisible life begins to crack.

chapters.title: Prayers with Teeth
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Word spreads through Ashvale's markets that a shrine idol wept blood and answered a beggar's prayer. The guild master, Vess Corvane, orders all god-touched goods seized. Petra witnesses a prayer answered firsthand and feels her stolen memories stir like sleeping animals. Emotional beat: awe laced with terror.

chapters.title: The Child Who Sold Herself
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. She traces the soul contract to Maren, a nine-year-old debt-orphan whose parents sold her soul to pay guild fees, payment due at the next dark moon. Maren doesn't understand what she lost. Petra, against every instinct for survival, pockets the original page. Emotional beat: guilt igniting into resolve.

chapters.title: What the Margins Remember
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Examining the contract's sigil, Petra recognizes her own handwriting in the authentication mark, a hand she shouldn't possess. A stolen memory surfaces: a courtroom beneath a mountain, a god-king's voice. Emotional beat: vertigo as her identity proves to be a forgery she wrote herself.

chapters.title: Vess Corvane's Kindness
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. The guild master privately offers Petra a promotion and protection, revealing she knows about the stolen page. Her generosity is a leash. She assigns Petra to 'recover' the contract, meaning destroy it and Maren's chance with it. Emotional beat: the seductive warmth of belonging, revealed as a trap.

chapters.title: The Thief Who Keeps Books
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra copies the entire ledger by memory into a hidden codex, an act of treason punishable by soul-forfeit. Her partner in the guild's lower ranks, the fence Odell, catches her and must choose whether to report her. Emotional beat: loyalty and truth pulling in opposite directions.

chapters.title: A God in the Alley
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. A ragged stranger in a fishmonger's alley knows Petra's true name, one even she doesn't remember. He claims to be a minor god, newly woken, who remembers her from before. He offers a way into the mountain court, at a price: a memory of her choosing. Emotional beat: temptation and the ache of an unlived past.

chapters.title: The Dark Moon Audit
chapters.summary: Multiple POV. The guild conducts its ritual audit; Petra must surrender her codex or be caught. Odell substitutes a forgery, sealing their complicity. Vess announces the soul-delivery will happen early, in three days. Emotional beat: the point of no return, crossed together.

chapters.title: Memories Are Currency
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. To pay the alley god, Petra surrenders her memory of her mother's face, discovering too late the memory was a key to her stolen past. The god opens a door in the mountain's roots. Emotional beat: sacrifice that costs more than promised.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: Petra's POV, with Odell. Petra and Odell descend through the mountain's abandoned mine-shafts into the court's antechambers, passing petitioners turned to salt. Odell confesses he once sold a memory too, and knows what she'll find below. Emotional beat: dread deepening into fellowship.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The court is a cathedral of contracts where the god-king, Aurelax, adjudicates debts in gold and grief. Petra poses as a guild auditor. She finds Maren's soul in a reliquary, small and flickering like a trapped moth. Emotional beat: horror at bureaucracy made divine.

chapters.title: Aurelax Remembers Her
chapters.summary: Aurelax's POV. The god-king recognizes Petra instantly, she was his first mortal clerk, who stole his ledger of names and fled with her own soul as payment. He offers her restoration: her memories, her name, her old power, if she delivers Maren's soul willingly. Emotional beat: corruption dressed as mercy.

chapters.title: The Price of a Name
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Restored memories flood back: she was Petra Dravenmoor before she was anyone, a god-touched child Aurelax hollowed out. She understands Vess was his agent all along. She pretends to accept his bargain. Emotional beat: rage crystallizing into strategy.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Counting House
chapters.summary: Odell's POV. Above ground, Vess discovers the forged codex and tortures Odell for Petra's location. Odell breaks, but gives Vess the wrong mountain pass, buying Petra hours. Emotional beat: loyalty proven at terrible cost.

chapters.title: The Reliquary Heist
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra steals Maren's soul from the reliquary vault using her memory-thief craft, unmaking the vault's wards by stealing their founding memories. Alarms of tolling bells shake the mountain. Emotional beat: triumph shadowed by pursuit.

chapters.title: What the Gods Owe
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The alley god intercepts her fleeing through the deep roads, revealing the waking gods chose her as their instrument against Aurelax, who has been devouring prayers for centuries. He asks her to destroy the court, not just the contract. Emotional beat: the weight of being a weapon.

chapters.title: Vess at the Gates
chapters.summary: Multiple POV. Vess's enforcers corner Petra at the mountain's gate. Vess offers Petra everything, guild, name, safety, if she hands over the soul. Petra refuses aloud, before witnesses, breaking Vess's power over her. Emotional beat: liberation through open defiance.

chapters.title: The Ledger Must Balance
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra realizes the contract can't be stolen, only unmade, and unmaking it requires a soul of equal weight. Hers. She returns to the court to offer the trade. Emotional beat: terrible arithmetic, accepted freely.

chapters.title: Aurelax's Court of Ash
chapters.summary: Petra's POV, climax. Petra offers her soul to void Maren's contract. Aurelax accepts, then betrays, moving to claim both. The waking gods answer the prayers of the salt-petitioners, and the court erupts. Petra seizes Aurelax's ledger of names and burns it, unmaking every contract, including her own. Emotional beat: the climax, sacrifice and rebellion fused.

chapters.title: Empty Pages
chapters.summary: Odell's POV. The mountain quiets. Odell carries a hollow-eyed Petra out of the ruins; she remembers nothing, not even him. Maren, soul restored, wakes whole in Ashvale. Vess, stripped of Aurelax's backing, faces the guild's justice. Emotional beat: grief and tenderness in the aftermath.

chapters.title: The First Answered Prayer
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. In a rebuilt Ashvale shrine, Maren prays for the woman who saved her. The waking gods, owing Petra a debt no ledger holds, return her memories, all of them, including the ones she chose to lose. Petra wakes weeping, whole, and known. Emotional beat: grace, unearned and accepted.

chapters.title: A New Sigil for Ashvale
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra founds a free ledger, a public record of every debt and contract in Ashvale, so no soul is ever sold in the dark again. Odell keeps the books beside her. The last entry is Maren's name, marked paid. Emotional beat: justice built outside the law, and a home at last.
